market_summary: The pre-market setup is cautious to risk-off, based on 1587 articles from Yahoo Finance, TradingView, The Motley Fool, CNBC Markets, Benzinga. The dominant theme is macro, with 637 macro items, 518 company items, 379 industry items, and 53 policy items. The tape looks more useful for identifying near-term rotation and risk appetite than for making a single directional index call.
market_narrative: US equities have a cautious to risk-off bias as Fed/rates, oil/energy, inflation dominate the information flow. Before the open, the setup still needs confirmation from futures, Treasury yields, opening breadth and pre-market volume.
index_performance_summary: Nasdaq and growth indexes should be the most sensitive part of the tape when AI, semiconductor, mega-cap tech, or guidance stories dominate. S&P 500 direction is likely to remain tied to Treasury yields, Fed expectations, inflation data, and broad risk appetite. Dow and equal-weight exposure may react more to policy, regulation, tariff, and industrial-cycle headlines.
macro_outlook: Macro coverage is concentrated around Fed/rates (144), inflation (89), oil/energy (81), growth/jobs (23). The practical implication is that equity rallies may need confirmation from rates and inflation expectations; if yields rise while growth headlines weaken, risk appetite can fade quickly.
risk_and_sentiment: Sentiment is cautious to risk-off: 125 positive, 204 negative, and 1258 neutral articles. My read is to avoid treating headline volume as conviction by itself; the more important signal is whether macro-sensitive and technology-sensitive stories are pointing in the same direction.
